/-!
# Erdős Problem 841

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/841](https://www.erdosproblems.com/841)
- [ErSe92] Erdős, Paul and Selfridge, J. L., Problems and Solutions: Solutions: 6655. Amer. Math.
  Monthly (1992), 791--794.
- [BPZ24] Bui, Hung M. and Pratt, Kyle and Zaharescu, Alexandru, A problem of
  Erdős-Graham-Granville-Selfridge on integral points on hyperelliptic curves. Math. Proc.
  Cambridge Philos. Soc. (2024), 309--323.
- [Gu04] Guy, Richard K., Unsolved problems in number theory. (2004), xviii+437.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Real Topology

namespace Erdos841

/-- `t n` is the least `T` such that `{n + 1, …, n + T}` contains a subset whose product with `n`
is a square; `t n = 0` if and only if `n` is itself a square. -/
noncomputable def t (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {T | ∃ J ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 T, IsSquare (n * ∏ j ∈ J, (n + j))}

open scoped Classical in
/--
Let $t_n$ be minimal such that $\{n+1,\ldots,n+t_n\}$ contains a subset whose product with $n$ is
a square number (and let $t_n=0$ if $n$ is itself square). Estimate $t_n$.

A problem of Erdős, Graham, and Selfridge. For example, $t_6=6$ since $6\cdot 8\cdot 12=24^2$. It
is trivial that $t_n\geq P(n)$, where $P(n)$ is the largest prime divisor of $n$.

Bui, Pratt, and Zaharescu [BPZ24] proved that the distribution of $t_n$ continues to follow
$P(n)$, in that for any fixed $c\in (0,1]$
$$\lim_{x\to \infty}\frac{\lvert \{ n\leq x : t_n\leq n^c\}\rvert}{x}
  = \lim_{x\to \infty}\frac{\lvert \{ n\leq x : P(n)\leq n^c\}\rvert}{x}.$$
The statement below is that the difference of the two counting functions is $o(x)$.

This was formalized in Lean by Codex.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos841/Core.lean#L16920"]
theorem erdos_841 (c : ℝ) (hc : c ∈ Set.Ioc 0 1) :
    Tendsto (fun x : ℕ ↦
      ((((Finset.Icc 1 x).filter fun n : ℕ ↦ (t n : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ c).card : ℝ) -
        ((Finset.Icc 1 x).filter fun n : ℕ ↦ (n.maxPrimeFac : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ c).card) / x)
      atTop (𝓝 0) := by
  sorry

/--
Selfridge proved that $t_n=P(n)$ if $P(n)>\sqrt{2n}+1$.

This was formalized in Lean by Codex.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos841/LowerBound.lean#L3183"]
theorem erdos_841.variants.selfridge_large_prime (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n)
    (h : √(2 * n) + 1 < (n.maxPrimeFac : ℝ)) : t n = n.maxPrimeFac := by
  sorry

/--
Selfridge proved that $t_n \ll n^{1/2}$ if $P(n)\leq\sqrt{2n}+1$.

This was formalized in Lean by Codex.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos841/Core.lean#L1373"]
theorem erdos_841.variants.selfridge_sqrt :
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ n : ℕ, (n.maxPrimeFac : ℝ) ≤ √(2 * n) + 1 → (t n : ℝ) ≤ C * √n := by
  sorry

open scoped Classical in
/--
Bui, Pratt, and Zaharescu [BPZ24] proved that for at least $x^{1-o(1)}$ many $n\leq x$ we have
$$t_n \leq \exp(O(\sqrt{\log n\log\log n})).$$

This was formalized in Lean by Codex.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos841/Core.lean#L16105"]
theorem erdos_841.variants.many_small_values : ∃ K : ℝ,
    Tendsto (fun x : ℕ ↦
      log (((Finset.Icc 1 x).filter fun n ↦
        (t n : ℝ) ≤ exp (K * √(log n * log (log n)))).card : ℝ) / log x) atTop (𝓝 1) := by
  sorry

/--
Bui, Pratt, and Zaharescu [BPZ24] proved that for all non-square $n$
$$t_n \gg (\log\log n)^{6/5}(\log\log\log n)^{-1/5}.$$

This was formalized in Lean by Codex.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos841/LowerBound.lean#L3166"]
theorem erdos_841.variants.lower_bound : ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ¬ IsSquare n →
      C * (log (log n) ^ ((6 : ℝ) / 5) * log (log (log n)) ^ (-(1 : ℝ) / 5)) ≤ t n := by
  sorry

end Erdos841

findings.description: The docstring at lines 49–50 claims unconditionally that t_n ≥ P(n), with P(n) the largest prime divisor. This is false under the file's correct definition of t: t 4 = 0 whereas Nat.maxPrimeFac 4 = 2. Both facts, and the failure of the universal inequality, were verified in scratch Lean without using the file's sorry-backed theorems. The erroneous inequality occurs only in the commentary; the distribution theorem itself is faithful.
findings.source_evidence: Bui–Pratt–Zaharescu [BPZ24], Lemma 3.4, states: “If P⁺(n)^2 ∤ n, then t_n ≥ P⁺(n).” Section 2 of the published article instead gives the unconditional comparison with P*(n), the largest prime dividing n to an odd power. See https://www.cambridge.org/core/product/identifier/S0305004123000488/type/journal_article .
findings.suggested_fix: Qualify the sentence with “whenever P(n)^2 ∤ n,” as in BPZ Lemma 3.4, or state the comparison with the largest prime occurring to an odd power, with an appropriate convention for squares. Do not change Nat.maxPrimeFac in the distribution theorem.

reformulations.difference: Lean states that the normalized difference of the two counting functions tends to zero, rather than explicitly asserting existence and equality of their separate limits.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: BPZ Remark 1 supplies the existing largest-prime-factor density, equal to ρ(1/c). Given that limit, (A(x)−B(x))/x → 0 is equivalent to A(x)/x tending to that same value. The generic equivalence under the known limit for B was proved in scratch Lean. Restricting x to natural numbers is harmless: the real-parameter counting functions are constant between consecutive integers and floor(x)/x tends to 1.

reformulations.difference: The qualitative x^{1−o(1)} many-small-values consequence of BPZ Theorem 1.2 is expressed as a limit of log(cardinality)/log x.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For the counted set M_K(x), 1 ≤ M_K(x) ≤ x whenever x ≥ 1: n=1 always qualifies, and the set is contained in [1,x]. Consequently log M_K(x)/log x → 1 is equivalent to: for every ε>0, eventually M_K(x) ≥ x^{1−ε}. This equivalence was proved for the actual counting function in scratch Lean. The outer existential fixes one constant K uniformly. BPZ Theorem 1.2 provides a stronger quantitative estimate, from which this documented qualitative corollary follows; the file does not claim its sharper constants.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses one real constant bounding every natural n in the small-largest-prime branch, instead of an asymptotic Vinogradov bound for positive n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: An eventual O(√n) bound extends to all positive n by increasing its constant to cover finitely many exceptions. Each t n is finite; scratch Lean proves the uniform elementary bound t n ≤ 3n. At n=0, t 0=0, so the added boundary case imposes no restriction. Requiring the constant to be positive would also be equivalent, since it may be increased.

review.notes: All six declarations were checked. Scratch files /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/log_equivalence.lean compile successfully and their verification lemmas use only standard Lean axioms. Checks include nonemptiness of the infimum's defining set, t n = 0 iff IsSquare n, small values t₂=4, t₃=5, t₅=5, t₆=6, t₁₄=7, and both asymptotic equivalences. The live Erdős page remained blocked by Cloudflare; mathematical comparisons used the primary papers, with the community database corroborating solved status. Guy was accessible in snippets and ErSe92 only bibliographically. The linked external proof statements match the file after identifying equivalent definitions; the external project was inspected but not independently rebuilt.
